category_values.description: The user has not specified their wheelchair use status
category_values.name: notSet

category_values.description: The user does not use a wheelchair
category_values.name: no

category_values.description: The user uses a wheelchair as their primary means of mobility
category_values.name: yes

HKCharacteristicTypeIdentifierWheelchair.short_description: Indicates whether the user uses a wheelchair, enabling appropriate activity tracking and metrics.

HKCorrelationTypeIdentifierBloodPressure.short_description: A correlation grouping systolic and diastolic blood pressure readings taken at the same time.

typical_range.notes:
Normal blood pressure is typically below 120/80 mmHg
diastolic: 60-80 mmHg
systolic: 90-120 mmHg

HKCorrelationTypeIdentifierFood.short_description: A correlation grouping nutritional data from a single food item or meal, including calories and nutrients.

typical_range.notes: Varies widely based on food item size and type

HKQuantityTypeIdentifierActiveEnergyBurn.short_description: Measures the energy expended through physical activity and movement above resting metabolic rate.

typical_range.notes: Highly variable based on activity level. Sedentary individuals may burn 150-300 kcal/day active; very active individuals can exceed 1500 kcal/day.

HKQuantityTypeIdentifierAppleExerciseTim.short_description: Measures the amount of time the user spent exercising at or above a brisk walk intensity.

typical_range.notes: Most users accumulate 0-60 minutes daily. Athletes or highly active individuals may exceed 120 minutes. Values above 180 minutes suggest extended training sessions or endurance activities.

HKQuantityTypeIdentifierAppleMoveTime.short_description: Measures the amount of time the user has spent performing activities involving full-body movements, primarily designed for wheelchair users.

typical_range.notes: Values depend on mobility level and activity patterns. Wheelchair users with active lifestyles may accumulate 120-300+ minutes daily. Sedentary periods will show lower values.

HKQuantityTypeIdentifierAppleSleepingWri.short_description: A relative measurement of wrist skin temperature deviation from a personal baseline, recorded during sleep by Apple Watch, used for menstrual cycle tracking and detecting physiological changes.

typical_range.notes: Typical nightly variation from personal baseline. Values represent deviation, not absolute temperature. Larger deviations may indicate illness or hormonal changes.

HKQuantityTypeIdentifierAppleStandTime.short_description: Measures the amount of time the user has spent standing throughout the day.

typical_range.notes: Typical values range from 60-180 minutes for sedentary individuals to 300+ minutes for active individuals. Maximum possible depends on waking hours and activity level.

HKQuantityTypeIdentifierAppleWalkingStea.short_description: Composite measure of walking stability and balance, used to estimate fall risk.

typical_range.notes: Scores are classified as OK (high steadiness), Low, or Very Low (highest fall risk).

HKQuantityTypeIdentifierAtrialFibrillati.short_description: An estimate of the percentage of time a person's heart shows signs of atrial fibrillation over a defined monitoring period.

typical_range.notes: 0% indicates no AFib detected; 100% indicates persistent/permanent AFib. Most paroxysmal AFib patients show intermittent burden.

HKQuantityTypeIdentifierBasalBodyTempera.short_description: The lowest body temperature attained during rest, typically measured immediately upon waking, used primarily for fertility awareness and ovulation tracking.

typical_range.notes: BBT typically ranges from 36.1-36.4 degC (97.0-97.5 degF) in the follicular phase and rises to 36.4-37.0 degC (97.5-98.6 degF) in the luteal phase after ovulation.

HKQuantityTypeIdentifierBasalEnergyBurne.short_description: Measures the resting energy expenditure (calories burned at rest) to maintain basic physiological functions.

typical_range.notes: Daily basal energy expenditure varies based on age, sex, height, weight, and body composition. Range represents typical adult values.

HKQuantityTypeIdentifierBloodAlcoholCont.short_description: Concentration of alcohol in blood, indicating intoxication level with legal and health implications

typical_range.notes: 0.08% is the legal driving limit in most US states; impairment begins at lower levels

HKQuantityTypeIdentifierBloodGlucose.short_description: The concentration of glucose in the blood, a key indicator for diabetes management and metabolic health.

typical_range.notes: Fasting typically 70-100 mg/dL; post-meal can rise to 140 mg/dL in non-diabetic individuals.

HKQuantityTypeIdentifierBloodPressureDia.short_description: The minimum arterial pressure between heartbeats when the heart relaxes, representing the lower number in a blood pressure reading.

typical_range.notes: Normal diastolic pressure ranges from 60-80 mmHg. Values above 120 mmHg indicate hypertensive crisis.

HKQuantityTypeIdentifierBloodPressureSys.short_description: The maximum arterial pressure during heart contraction, representing the upper number in a blood pressure reading.

typical_range.notes: Normal systolic pressure ranges from 90-120 mmHg. Values above 180 mmHg indicate hypertensive crisis.

HKQuantityTypeIdentifierBodyFatPercentag.short_description: The proportion of total body mass composed of adipose tissue, expressed as a percentage.

typical_range.notes: Essential fat minimum is approximately 3% for men and 10-12% for women; values above 50% indicate severe obesity.

HKQuantityTypeIdentifierBodyMass.short_description: The user's total body weight, typically measured using a scale.

typical_range.notes: Adult range typically 40-150 kg; extreme values outside 20-300 kg should be validated for data entry errors.

HKQuantityTypeIdentifierBodyMassIndex.short_description: A calculated ratio of weight to height used to classify weight status and assess health risks.

typical_range.notes: Extreme values outside 10-60 are physiologically implausible for adults; typical adult range is 15-40.

HKQuantityTypeIdentifierBodyTemperature.short_description: A measurement of the body's internal temperature, a fundamental vital sign indicating metabolic and immune system status.

typical_range.notes: Normal oral temperature range for healthy adults. Values vary by measurement site and individual baseline.

HKQuantityTypeIdentifierCyclingCadence.short_description: Measures pedal revolutions per minute (RPM) during cycling.

typical_range.notes: Most cyclists naturally pedal between 60-100 RPM. Trained cyclists typically maintain 85-100 RPM. Professional cyclists may sustain 100-110 RPM. Sprints can briefly exceed 120-150 RPM. Low cadence (<60) common during climbing or heavy resistance.

HKQuantityTypeIdentifierCyclingFunctiona.short_description: Represents the maximum power a cyclist can sustain for approximately one hour.

typical_range.notes: FTP varies dramatically by fitness, training, and body size. Untrained individuals may have FTP of 100-150W. Recreational cyclists typically 150-250W. Well-trained amateurs 250-350W. Elite professionals can exceed 400-450W. Female values typically 10-15% lower at same training level.

HKQuantityTypeIdentifierCyclingPower.short_description: Measures the instantaneous power output during cycling in watts.

typical_range.notes: Highly variable by fitness, effort level, and duration. Recreational cyclists may average 100-150W on easy rides. Trained amateurs average 200-300W. Elite professionals can sustain 400+ watts and sprint to 1500-2000W.

HKQuantityTypeIdentifierCyclingSpeed.short_description: Measures the instantaneous speed during cycling activities.

typical_range.notes: Equivalent to 0-90 km/h (0-56 mph). Recreational cyclists typically average 15-25 km/h (4-7 m/s). Trained cyclists average 25-35 km/h (7-10 m/s). Professional sprints can exceed 70 km/h (19 m/s). Descents may reach 80-100+ km/h.

HKQuantityTypeIdentifierDietaryBiotin.short_description: Records dietary intake of biotin (vitamin B7), essential for carboxylase enzymes in fatty acid, amino acid, and glucose metabolism.

HKQuantityTypeIdentifierDietaryCaffeine.short_description: Total caffeine consumed from beverages, food, and supplements, measured in milligrams.

HKQuantityTypeIdentifierDietaryCalcium.short_description: Calcium intake from food and supplements, essential for bone health and muscle function.

HKQuantityTypeIdentifierDietaryCarbohydr.short_description: Total carbohydrate intake including sugars, starches, and fiber

typical_range.notes: Highly variable based on dietary approach. Ketogenic diets may target <50g; endurance athletes may exceed 500g on heavy training days.

HKQuantityTypeIdentifierDietaryChloride.short_description: Chloride intake from food and supplements, essential for fluid balance, gastric acid production, and nerve transmission.

typical_range.notes: Vegans consume 0mg; average American intake is 250-350mg/day. Single egg yolk contains ~186mg.

HKQuantityTypeIdentifierDietaryChromium.short_description: Chromium intake from food and supplements, involved in insulin signaling and macronutrient metabolism.

HKQuantityTypeIdentifierDietaryCopper.short_description: Copper intake from food and supplements, essential for iron metabolism, connective tissue, and nervous system function.

HKQuantityTypeIdentifierDietaryEnergyCon.short_description: Total caloric energy intake from food and beverages

typical_range.notes: Highly variable based on age, sex, body size, activity level, and metabolic health. Athletes may exceed 5000 kcal/day.

HKQuantityTypeIdentifierDietaryFatMonoun.short_description: Monounsaturated fatty acid intake, primarily from olive oil, nuts, and avocados

typical_range.notes: Mediterranean diet provides 15-20% of calories from MUFA. Average American intake is ~11-12% of calories.

HKQuantityTypeIdentifierDietaryFatPolyun.short_description: Polyunsaturated fatty acid intake including omega-3 and omega-6 essential fatty acids

typical_range.notes: Average intake is 5-10% of calories. Western diets are often imbalanced with omega-6:omega-3 ratios of 15-20:1 (optimal: 4:1 or lower).

HKQuantityTypeIdentifierDietaryFatSatura.short_description: Saturated fatty acid intake from animal and tropical plant sources

typical_range.notes: Average American intake is 11-12% of calories (~25-30g). Recommendations target <10% of calories (<22g on 2000 kcal).

HKQuantityTypeIdentifierDietaryFatTotal.short_description: Total fat intake from all dietary sources

typical_range.notes: On a 2000 kcal diet, 44-78g represents 20-35% of calories. Ketogenic diets may reach 150-200g/day.

HKQuantityTypeIdentifierDietaryFiber.short_description: Total fiber intake from plant-based foods and supplements

typical_range.notes: Most Americans consume only 10-15g/day, well below recommendations. High-fiber diets may exceed 40g/day.

HKQuantityTypeIdentifierDietaryFolate.short_description: Records dietary intake of folate (vitamin B9), essential for DNA synthesis, cell division, and neural tube development.

HKQuantityTypeIdentifierDietaryIodine.short_description: Iodine intake from food and supplements, essential for thyroid hormone synthesis and metabolic regulation.

HKQuantityTypeIdentifierDietaryIron.short_description: Iron intake from food and supplements, essential for oxygen transport and energy metabolism.

HKQuantityTypeIdentifierDietaryMagnesium.short_description: Magnesium intake from food and supplements, essential for energy metabolism, muscle function, and bone health.

HKQuantityTypeIdentifierDietaryManganese.short_description: Manganese intake from food and supplements, essential for bone formation, metabolism, and antioxidant defense.

HKQuantityTypeIdentifierDietaryMolybdenu.short_description: Molybdenum intake from food and supplements, essential as a cofactor for enzymes involved in sulfur metabolism.

HKQuantityTypeIdentifierDietaryNiacin.short_description: Records dietary intake of niacin (vitamin B3), essential for energy metabolism, DNA repair, and cellular signaling.

HKQuantityTypeIdentifierDietaryPantothen.short_description: Records dietary intake of pantothenic acid (vitamin B5), essential for coenzyme A synthesis and acyl carrier protein function.

HKQuantityTypeIdentifierDietaryPhosphoru.short_description: Phosphorus intake from food and supplements, essential for bone structure, energy metabolism, and cellular function.

HKQuantityTypeIdentifierDietaryPotassium.short_description: Potassium intake from food and supplements, essential for fluid balance, nerve transmission, and muscle contraction.

HKQuantityTypeIdentifierDietaryProtein.short_description: Total protein intake from food and supplements

typical_range.notes: Varies significantly by body weight, activity level, and health goals. Athletes and those in caloric deficit may consume 2-3g/kg body weight.

HKQuantityTypeIdentifierDietaryRiboflavi.short_description: Records dietary intake of riboflavin (vitamin B2), essential for energy production and antioxidant function.

HKQuantityTypeIdentifierDietarySelenium.short_description: Selenium intake from food and supplements, essential for antioxidant defense, thyroid function, and immune health.

HKQuantityTypeIdentifierDietarySodium.short_description: Sodium intake from food, beverages, and table salt

typical_range.notes: Average American intake is 3400mg/day, well above the 2300mg guideline. Processed foods contribute 70%+ of intake.

HKQuantityTypeIdentifierDietarySugar.short_description: Total sugar intake including natural and added sugars

typical_range.notes: Average American consumes 60-80g/day of added sugars alone. WHO recommends limiting added sugars to <25g/day.

HKQuantityTypeIdentifierDietaryThiamin.short_description: Records dietary intake of thiamin (vitamin B1), essential for carbohydrate metabolism and neurological function.

HKQuantityTypeIdentifierDietaryVitaminA.short_description: Fat-soluble vitamin essential for vision, immune function, and cellular growth

HKQuantityTypeIdentifierDietaryVitaminB1.short_description: Water-soluble vitamin essential for DNA synthesis, neurological function, and red blood cell formation

HKQuantityTypeIdentifierDietaryVitaminB6.short_description: Water-soluble vitamin essential for amino acid metabolism, neurotransmitter synthesis, and hemoglobin formation

HKQuantityTypeIdentifierDietaryVitaminC.short_description: Water-soluble antioxidant essential for collagen synthesis, immune function, and iron absorption

HKQuantityTypeIdentifierDietaryVitaminD.short_description: Fat-soluble vitamin essential for calcium absorption, bone health, immune function, and cellular regulation

HKQuantityTypeIdentifierDietaryVitaminE.short_description: Fat-soluble antioxidant protecting cell membranes from oxidative damage

HKQuantityTypeIdentifierDietaryVitaminK.short_description: Fat-soluble vitamin essential for blood clotting and bone metabolism

HKQuantityTypeIdentifierDietaryWater.short_description: Total water consumed from beverages and food, measured in milliliters or liters.

HKQuantityTypeIdentifierDietaryZinc.short_description: Zinc intake from food and supplements, essential for immune function, wound healing, and protein synthesis.

HKQuantityTypeIdentifierDistanceCycling.short_description: Measures the distance the user has moved by cycling.

typical_range.notes: Daily values vary widely from 0 for non-cyclists to 50+ km for commuters and recreational riders. Competitive cyclists may log 100-200+ km in training rides. Century rides (160 km/100 mi) represent common endurance goals.

HKQuantityTypeIdentifierDistanceDownhill.short_description: Measures the distance traveled while skiing or snowboarding downhill.

typical_range.notes: Single-day values vary enormously based on terrain, conditions, and skier/snowboarder ability. Recreational skiers might cover 15-30 km per day; avid skiers can exceed 50 km on a full day.

HKQuantityTypeIdentifierDistanceSwimming.short_description: Measures the distance the user has moved by swimming.

typical_range.notes: Single session values typically range from 500m for casual swimmers to 4000m+ for competitive training. Open water swims can extend to marathon distances (10km+). Daily totals vary widely based on swim frequency.

HKQuantityTypeIdentifierDistanceWalkingR.short_description: Measures the distance the user has moved by walking or running.

typical_range.notes: Daily values typically range from 2-10 km for most adults. Values above 20 km/day are uncommon except for runners, hikers, or occupations requiring extensive walking. Marathon distance (42.2 km) represents an upper extreme for single-day values.

HKQuantityTypeIdentifierDistanceWheelcha.short_description: Measures the distance the user has moved using a wheelchair.

typical_range.notes: Daily values vary widely based on mobility level, activity type, and environment accessibility. Active wheelchair users may travel 2-10 km daily. Wheelchair athletes in training may exceed 20 km.

HKQuantityTypeIdentifierElectrodermalAct.short_description: Skin conductance measurement indicating sympathetic nervous system arousal and stress response

typical_range.notes: Baseline varies significantly between individuals; relative changes are more clinically meaningful than absolute values

HKQuantityTypeIdentifierEnvironmentalAud.short_description: Ambient sound level exposure measured in A-weighted decibels (dB(A)), indicating potential hearing damage risk from environmental noise.

HKQuantityTypeIdentifierEnvironmentalSou.short_description: Amount of environmental noise reduced by active noise cancellation in compatible earbuds, measured in decibels (dB).

HKQuantityTypeIdentifierFlightsClimbed.short_description: Counts the number of flights of stairs climbed, where one flight equals approximately 10 feet (3 meters) of elevation gain.

typical_range.notes: Highly dependent on living/working environment. Office workers in single-story buildings may record 0-5; those in multi-story buildings or hilly areas can easily exceed 20.

HKQuantityTypeIdentifierForcedExpiratory.short_description: Volume of air forcefully exhaled in the first second of spirometry, a key indicator of obstructive lung disease

typical_range.notes: Highly dependent on age, sex, height, and ethnicity; interpret using percent predicted values

HKQuantityTypeIdentifierForcedVitalCapac.short_description: Total volume of air forcefully exhaled after maximum inhalation, essential for assessing lung capacity and restrictive diseases

typical_range.notes: Varies significantly with age, sex, height, and ethnicity; interpret using percent predicted values

HKQuantityTypeIdentifierHeadphoneAudioEx.short_description: Audio level exposure from headphones and earbuds measured in A-weighted decibels (dB(A)), tracking personal listening habits for hearing protection.

HKQuantityTypeIdentifierHeartRate.short_description: Measures the number of times the heart beats per minute.

typical_range.notes: Range encompasses bradycardia through maximum exercise heart rates. Values outside this range are physiologically rare but possible.

HKQuantityTypeIdentifierHeartRateRecover.short_description: Measures the reduction in heart rate from peak exercise intensity to one minute after exercise cessation, a powerful indicator of cardiovascular fitness and autonomic function.

typical_range.notes: Range varies by fitness level, exercise intensity, and individual physiology. Very fit individuals may show recovery >50 bpm while those with cardiac conditions may show <12 bpm.

HKQuantityTypeIdentifierHeartRateVariabi.short_description: Measures the root mean square of successive differences between normal heartbeat intervals (RMSSD), a short-term heart rate variability metric that mainly reflects vagal (parasympathetic) activity; the Health app calls it Recovery HRV.

typical_range.notes: Covers most healthy adults at rest in short recordings: 5-minute resting means fall from about 40 ms at 25-34 to about 19 ms at 65-74 (Voss 2015), and pooled studies report a mean of 42 ms (Nunan 2010). Higher values are common in young and endurance-trained people. Values depend heavily on age, posture, time of day and breathing, so compare against the person's own baseline.

HKQuantityTypeIdentifierHeartRateVariabi.short_description: Measures the standard deviation of normal-to-normal heartbeat intervals, reflecting autonomic nervous system function and overall physiological resilience.

typical_range.notes: Apple Watch typically reports short-term SDNN measurements (not 24-hour SDNN). Values vary dramatically by age, fitness, and measurement duration. Context is critical for interpretation.

HKQuantityTypeIdentifierHeight.short_description: A measurement of the user's standing height, a fundamental anthropometric parameter used for health assessment, growth monitoring, and clinical calculations.

typical_range.notes: Range encompasses newborns through exceptionally tall adults. Adult heights typically fall between 1.50-2.00 m (4'11" - 6'7").

HKQuantityTypeIdentifierInhalerUsage.short_description: Count of inhaler actuations for asthma and COPD management tracking

typical_range.notes: Per day; rescue inhaler use >2 times/week (excluding pre-exercise use) suggests suboptimal asthma control

HKQuantityTypeIdentifierInsulinDelivery.short_description: Amount of insulin delivered for diabetes management, tracking basal and bolus doses in international units

typical_range.notes: Total daily dose varies widely; typically 0.5-1.0 IU/kg body weight for Type 1 diabetes

HKQuantityTypeIdentifierLeanBodyMass.short_description: The total body mass minus all fat tissue, including muscle, bone, organs, and water.

typical_range.notes: Adult lean body mass typically ranges from 35-80 kg depending on sex, height, and muscularity.

HKQuantityTypeIdentifierNikeFuel.short_description: A proprietary Nike activity metric that quantifies overall physical activity into a single numeric score (largely deprecated).

typical_range.notes: Daily NikeFuel targets varied by user; 2000-3000 NikeFuel was considered a moderate daily goal during the metric's active period. Elite athletes could exceed 5000 NikeFuel daily.

HKQuantityTypeIdentifierNumberOfAlcoholi.short_description: Count of standard alcoholic drinks consumed, used to track alcohol intake for health monitoring.

HKQuantityTypeIdentifierNumberOfTimesFal.short_description: Cumulative count of detected fall events for fall risk assessment and elderly health monitoring

typical_range.notes: Per year for community-dwelling adults; any fall warrants clinical evaluation in older adults

HKQuantityTypeIdentifierOxygenSaturation.short_description: The percentage of hemoglobin in the blood that is saturated with oxygen.

typical_range.notes: For healthy individuals at sea level. Values may be lower at high altitude or in certain medical conditions.

HKQuantityTypeIdentifierPeakExpiratoryFl.short_description: Maximum speed of exhalation measuring airway patency, essential for asthma self-monitoring and action plan guidance

typical_range.notes: Highly variable by age, sex, and height; personal best is the key reference value

HKQuantityTypeIdentifierPeripheralPerfus.short_description: A measure of peripheral blood flow derived from pulse oximetry, representing the ratio of pulsatile to non-pulsatile blood components.

typical_range.notes: Normal range typically 0.5-2.0% in healthy adults at rest. Values vary significantly based on measurement site, temperature, and physiological state.

HKQuantityTypeIdentifierPhysicalEffort.short_description: Measures the perceived intensity of physical activity on a standardized effort scale.

typical_range.notes: Values roughly correspond to MET values. Resting is ~1.0, walking ~3-4, running ~8-12, and maximum effort activities can reach 15-20 for elite athletes.

HKQuantityTypeIdentifierPushCount.short_description: Measures the number of wheelchair pushes performed by the user for mobility and exercise.

typical_range.notes: Daily push counts vary significantly based on activity level, wheelchair type, and environmental factors. Active wheelchair users typically perform 3,000-8,000 pushes per day. Wheelchair athletes in training may exceed 10,000 pushes daily.

HKQuantityTypeIdentifierRespiratoryRate.short_description: The number of breaths taken per minute, typically measured during sleep.

typical_range.notes: Range for healthy adults at rest. Values may vary during sleep, exercise, or illness.

HKQuantityTypeIdentifierRestingHeartRate.short_description: Measures the heart rate while the user is at rest and relaxed, typically the lowest heart rate during waking hours.

typical_range.notes: Encompasses athletic bradycardia through elevated resting rates seen in deconditioned or unwell individuals

HKQuantityTypeIdentifierRunningGroundCon.short_description: The duration each foot spends in contact with the ground during a running stride.

typical_range.notes: Elite sprinters show 160-180 ms; elite distance runners 180-220 ms; recreational runners 220-280 ms; slower joggers 260-320+ ms. Ground contact time decreases as running speed increases.

HKQuantityTypeIdentifierRunningPower.short_description: The rate of mechanical work performed during running, measured in watts.

typical_range.notes: Highly dependent on body weight, running speed, and terrain. Recreational runners typically see 200-300W at easy pace; elite runners may sustain 350-450W during races.

HKQuantityTypeIdentifierRunningSpeed.short_description: The rate of travel during running activities, typically measured in meters per second or minutes per mile/kilometer.

typical_range.notes: 2.0 m/s = 13:24 min/mile (slow jog); 4.0 m/s = 6:42 min/mile (moderate run); 6.5 m/s = 4:07 min/mile (elite pace). Walking is typically 1.0-1.8 m/s.

HKQuantityTypeIdentifierRunningStrideLen.short_description: The distance covered in a single running stride, measured from one foot contact to the next contact of the same foot.

typical_range.notes: Stride length varies significantly with running speed, height, and running form. Jogging typically produces 1.2-1.6m strides; moderate running 1.6-2.0m; fast running 2.0-2.8m. Elite sprinters can exceed 3m.

HKQuantityTypeIdentifierRunningVerticalO.short_description: The amount of vertical bounce or up-and-down movement during each running stride.

typical_range.notes: Elite runners typically exhibit 6-8 cm; recreational runners commonly show 8-12 cm. Values above 12-14 cm suggest inefficient form. Vertical oscillation tends to increase with speed but efficient runners minimize this increase.

HKQuantityTypeIdentifierSixMinuteWalkTes.short_description: Total distance walked during a standardized six-minute walk test, a validated measure of functional capacity.

typical_range.notes: Healthy adults typically achieve 400-700 m; cardiac/pulmonary patients often 200-400 m.

HKQuantityTypeIdentifierStairAscentSpeed.short_description: Speed of climbing stairs, measuring vertical velocity during stair ascent.

typical_range.notes: Healthy adults typically achieve 0.4-0.6 m/s; values <0.3 m/s indicate functional limitation.

HKQuantityTypeIdentifierStairDescentSpee.short_description: Speed of descending stairs, measuring vertical velocity during stair descent.

typical_range.notes: Healthy adults typically achieve 0.5-0.8 m/s; descent is usually faster than ascent in healthy individuals.

HKQuantityTypeIdentifierStepCount.short_description: Measures the number of steps the user has taken.

typical_range.notes: Daily values typically range from 2,000-15,000 steps for most adults. Values above 25,000 are uncommon but possible for ultramarathon athletes or occupations requiring extensive walking.

HKQuantityTypeIdentifierSwimmingStrokeCo.short_description: Measures the number of strokes performed while swimming.

typical_range.notes: Single workout values depend heavily on distance and stroke efficiency. A typical 1500m workout might involve 900-1500 strokes depending on swimmer skill level. Competitive swimmers are more efficient (fewer strokes per lap) than recreational swimmers.

HKQuantityTypeIdentifierTimeInDaylight.short_description: Duration of exposure to outdoor daylight conditions, measured in minutes, relevant for circadian rhythm regulation, mental health, and eye health.

HKQuantityTypeIdentifierUVExposure.short_description: Ultraviolet radiation exposure measurement for skin cancer risk assessment and vitamin D synthesis tracking

typical_range.notes: UV Index scale: 0-2 Low, 3-5 Moderate, 6-7 High, 8-10 Very High, 11+ Extreme

HKQuantityTypeIdentifierUnderwaterDepth.short_description: Measures the user's depth underwater during diving activities.

typical_range.notes: Apple Watch Ultra rated for recreational diving to 40m (130 ft). Most recreational dives occur between 10-30m. Surface is 0m. Values above 40m exceed device rating and most recreational diving certification limits.

HKQuantityTypeIdentifierVO2Max.short_description: Maximum oxygen uptake during exercise, a key indicator of cardiorespiratory fitness.

typical_range.notes: Wide variation based on age, sex, and fitness level. Elite endurance athletes may exceed 70-80 mL/kg/min. Sedentary adults typically range 25-40 mL/kg/min.

HKQuantityTypeIdentifierWaistCircumferen.short_description: A measurement of the circumference of the waist at the level of the umbilicus or narrowest point, a key indicator of central adiposity and cardiometabolic risk.

typical_range.notes: Range encompasses children through adults with severe obesity. Healthy adult range typically 60-100 cm.

HKQuantityTypeIdentifierWalkingAsymmetry.short_description: Percentage difference in step time between left and right legs during walking.

typical_range.notes: Healthy adults typically show <10% asymmetry; values >15% warrant clinical evaluation.

HKQuantityTypeIdentifierWalkingDoubleSup.short_description: Percentage of the gait cycle when both feet are simultaneously in contact with the ground.

typical_range.notes: Healthy adults typically show 20-30% double support; values above 35% may indicate balance concerns.

HKQuantityTypeIdentifierWalkingHeartRate.short_description: Measures the user's average heart rate while walking, providing insight into cardiovascular fitness during light activity.

typical_range.notes: Range varies significantly based on walking pace, terrain, fitness level, and age. Brisk walking elevates heart rate more than casual walking.

HKQuantityTypeIdentifierWalkingSpeed.short_description: Average speed during walking, a key indicator of functional mobility and overall health status.

typical_range.notes: Healthy adults typically walk 1.2-1.4 m/s; values below 0.8 m/s are clinically significant.

HKQuantityTypeIdentifierWalkingStepLengt.short_description: Average distance covered with each step during walking, a fundamental gait parameter.

typical_range.notes: Varies significantly with height; typical range is 65-85 cm for average height adults.

HKQuantityTypeIdentifierWaterTemperature.short_description: Measures the temperature of the water during swimming or diving activities.

typical_range.notes: Apple Watch Ultra operates in water temperatures from 0°C to 40°C. Typical recreational water temperatures range from 15-30°C. Cold water (<15°C) and very warm water (>35°C) present specific physiological considerations.
